title: Suggested challenges and spotlights
summary: The console suggests the next challenge from the team's own numbers, and Arena spotlights notable moments itself.
changes: Suggested challenges: up to three chips above the challenge list, each with the reason on hover. Escalations over 5%, evaluation average under 85, low customer sentiment, adherence under 90%, scarce kudos, or a team points target when all is well. Click one and the form opens filled in.

Spotlights: a 95%+ evaluation, day 5, 10, 20 or 50 of a quality streak, or a personal best day is posted to the team's kudos feed, the wallboard ticker and the team's Slack or Teams channel as a spotlight from Arena. No points attached. A spotlights switch in the notifications card turns them off per team.
upgrade: No action is needed. Spotlights are on by default for teams with a channel; switch them off in the notifications card if you prefer.

title: People from the console, and your data in your warehouse
summary: Supervisors manage sign-ins from a People button, and per-agent per-day rows flow to a warehouse as nightly files or through a read API with data keys.
changes: People: a button at the top of the console lists everyone in the stack's user pool, adds a person (pick the Connect agent, choose agent or supervisor, optional email for the invitation), changes roles, resets passwords and removes sign-ins. No command line needed. With an external identity provider the console says so.

Warehouse export: with the new DataExport setting enabled, the stack writes yesterday's per-agent rows every night to a private export bucket as newline JSON under days/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/, one file per team, with a manifest. Databricks Auto Loader and Athena read it as-is.

Read API: a Data button in the console mints data keys; a warehouse or BI tool then reads the same rows over HTTPS at /api/data/<key>/days?from&to without a sign-in. Keys are shown once, expire after a year and can be revoked.
Signed-in supervisors can read the same rows at /api/export/days.
upgrade: No action is needed. Set DataExport to enabled when you update the stack if you want the nightly files; the read API and People work as soon as the stack is updated.
The People button needs the stack's own Cognito pool (the default AuthMode).

title: Leaderboard opt-out and a security write-up for reviewers
summary: An agent can keep themselves off teammates' boards and wallboards, and the help center now has a full security and architecture write-up for the people who review software before a centre may use it.
changes: Hide me from others: a tick box in the agent panel removes the agent from teammates' leaderboards, wallboards and the standings teammates see. Supervisors still see everyone, marked "hidden" in the console, and the agent still sees themselves.

Security and your data: the help center article is now a complete write-up covering architecture, what is stored, what leaves the account, who sees what, least privilege per function, encryption, retention, deletion and shared responsibility. Linked from every page footer and the pricing FAQ.
upgrade: No action is needed.

title: Your own reward catalog, and balances that reset
summary: Supervisors edit the rewards on offer per team, and agents spend from a balance that resets weekly, monthly or quarterly so newcomers can catch up.
changes: Reward catalog: a Catalog button on the console's reward approvals card edits the rewards and their point costs, up to 20 per team, with a one-click return to the default catalog.

Balance period: choose whether spendable balances reset every week, month or quarter. A balance is the points earned in the period minus rewards approved in it. Earned points, levels and leaderboards are unchanged.
The agent panel shows the balance, the period and the reset date, and lists the team's own catalog.
Approving a reward no longer subtracts from the agent's weekly points; it is recorded against their balance instead, so leaderboards show what was earned.
upgrade: No action is needed. Every team starts on the default catalog with weekly balances, which matches how rewards worked before.
Rewards approved before this update were subtracted from weekly points at the time; they are not re-counted against the new balances.

title: History on day one, evaluation acknowledgements, and a free trial
summary: A new stack loads the last 90 days from Amazon Connect, agents earn points for acknowledging their evaluations, and the first 30 days are free for up to 25 agents a day.
changes: Backfill: with ConnectInstanceArn set, the stack lists your users so the whole team appears in the console, and loads up to 90 days of contacts handled, handle time and evaluation scores per agent from Connect's historical metrics. Points are what Arena would have scored. Days the stream already covered are left alone, and backfilled days never count toward billing.

Evaluation acknowledgements: 5 points, scaled by the quality weight, when an agent acknowledges their evaluation in Amazon Connect. The stack checks hourly for evaluations submitted in the last 30 days.
Free trial: for 30 days from the first nightly usage report, up to 25 active agents a day are not billed. The full count is still recorded.
The agent's feed names acknowledgement and history lines.
upgrade: Existing stacks keep running as before. To load history, set ConnectInstanceArn when you update the stack; BackfillDays defaults to 90 and the load runs once within the hour.
The trial clock starts with the first usage report after this update, so existing subscribers also get 30 days of allowance.
Acknowledgement points need EvaluationsBucket set, as evaluation scoring already does.

title: Scoring profiles per team and a personal-best view
summary: Each team can be scored on its own mix, and an agent can choose to measure against their own record instead of the team.
changes: Per-team scoring profiles: the console's scoring mix card now saves for every team (the default) or for this team only, shows which one applies, and can put a team back on the default. Every event is scored with its team's mix.

Personal-best mode: a tick box above the leaderboard in the agent panel swaps the team board for the agent's own record: today against their best day, this week against their best week, and their average active day. The header shows the percentage of their best day instead of a rank. The choice is saved on the agent's profile.
The agent's points feed names schedule adherence lines with the percentage.
upgrade: No action is needed. The existing mix becomes the default for every team; no team has its own profile until a supervisor saves one.
Personal-best mode reads the agent's day rows, which the stack keeps for 90 days, so records go back at most that far.

title: Schedule adherence, reward budgets, and your own time zone
summary: Adherence from Amazon Connect now earns points, each team can carry a monthly reward budget, and every day in Arena starts at midnight where your centre is.
changes: Schedule adherence: with the new ScheduleAdherence setting enabled, Arena reads yesterday's adherence for every agent from Amazon Connect each night and awards 5 points per hour spent on schedule, weighted by the adherence slider. Agents without a schedule that day get nothing and lose nothing.
Adherence is a measure for races and head-to-heads, shows in each agent's feed with the percentage and hours, and appears as a team average in the results report.

Monthly reward budget per team, set from the Budget button on the console's reward approvals card. An approval that would go over the budget is refused and the request stays pending. The card shows how much of the month is used.
Budget alerts in Slack, Teams and the digest channels at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% of the month's budget, under the reward requests switch.

Timezone setting: days, weeks and months now start at local midnight for points, streaks, challenge dates, the digest hour and budgets. Before this release everything rolled over at midnight UTC, which cut a US evening shift's work in two.
The streak job now runs hourly and acts once per local day, so streak bonuses arrive after your midnight rather than after UTC midnight.
upgrade: Set Timezone when you update the stack. Day and week totals from before the change were keyed to UTC days and stay as they are; new totals start from the change. A change made at the end of a shift is least noticeable.

To score adherence, set ScheduleAdherence to enabled. Your Connect instance needs forecasting, capacity planning and scheduling enabled; without them the nightly import finds no schedules and writes nothing.
Budgets are off until a supervisor sets one, so nothing changes about approvals unless you choose to.

title: Notifications, contest rules, and head-to-head
summary: Arena now reaches the team in Slack, Teams and email, challenges have real rules and prizes, and agents can go head-to-head or team against team.
changes: Slack and Microsoft Teams: kudos, reward requests and decisions, challenge starts and results are posted to a channel per team, set up from the console with a test button.
Daily digest: team points, contacts, evaluation average, sentiment, kudos, the top five, open challenges and what needs attention, at the hour you choose, to Slack, Teams or email.

Agent race: a ranked challenge on one or two weighted measures, with a minimum number of contacts to qualify, prizes for 1st, 2nd and 3rd, the option to hide names until it ends, and a supervisor switch to disqualify or reinstate an agent.
Head-to-head: two agents on one measure, winner takes the reward. Team vs team: your team against another routing profile on one measure.
Challenges are now measured over their whole period, not just today. When one ends its standings are frozen and prizes are paid as points, once, with a line in each winner's feed.
The agent panel shows where you stand in a race and what you would win.
upgrade: No action is needed. Existing challenges keep running and finish with frozen results.
To receive the email digest, set the new DigestEmail setting on the stack and accept the confirmation email AWS sends. Slack and Teams need no stack change: paste the webhook into the console.

title: Tighter access, honest kudos, and discreet wallboards
summary: Agents now see only their own team and their own feed, kudos are capped and cannot be traded, and wallboards can show shortened names.
changes: Agents can read only their own team's leaderboard, challenges, rewards, kudos feed and coaching plans, and only their own points feed. Supervisors keep access to every team.
Kudos are limited per sender per day (five by default), cannot be sent to yourself, and must go to a teammate. An agent receiving far more kudos than the team average is flagged in the console.
A new setting, WallboardNames, shows full names, first name and last initial, or initials only on sign-in-free wallboards. Signed-in pages always show full names.
The database now keeps 35 days of point-in-time backups.
upgrade: No action is needed; existing settings keep their behaviour.

If you use your own identity provider (AuthMode external), its tokens must carry the custom:team and custom:agentArn claims, as the sign-in guide already requires. Agents without a team claim are now refused on team pages.
Set KudosDailyLimit to change the cap, and WallboardNames to first or initials for floor TVs in shared spaces.

title: Quality on every contact, a results report, and coaching
summary: Arena now measures quality on every analysed contact, shows whether things are improving, and turns a flag into an agreed action.
changes: Customer sentiment: each contact analysed by Contact Lens earns points from the customer's overall sentiment. It never deducts points.
Survey scores: post-contact survey answers earn points, read from Connect contact records or sent by an outside survey tool.
New flag for an agent whose customer sentiment stays low across several contacts.
Results report: compares the last 7, 14, 30 or 90 days with the period before, for the team and for each agent, with a daily chart, CSV export and a print layout.

Coaching plans: open a plan from any flag with an agreed action, a follow-up date and a private supervisor note. The agent confirms it in their panel, and the console shows the numbers before and since.
The supervisor console and agent panel show customer sentiment and survey score alongside the evaluation average.
upgrade: No action is needed to keep existing behaviour.
To score customer sentiment, set the new AnalysisBucket setting to the bucket Connect writes Contact Lens analysis to, and turn on EventBridge notifications for that bucket.
To score survey answers from Connect, send contact records to the Arena stream and set CsatAttribute to the contact attribute your survey writes.

title: AWS Marketplace license integration
summary: Arena moved to the current AWS Marketplace integration for software subscriptions.
changes: A subscription is now identified by its AWS Marketplace license, and usage is reported against that license.
Billing unit changed to the active agent-day: one unit for each agent with scored activity on a day.
The registration page passes the license and AWS account to the stack automatically when you launch.
upgrade: Stack settings changed: MarketplaceLicenseArn and MarketplaceCustomerAccountId replace MarketplaceCustomerId. Launch from the registration page so they are filled in for you.

title: One-click setup and operations
summary: Arena installs its own pages and looks after itself in production.
changes: Registration page: subscribe on AWS Marketplace and launch Arena into your account from one link.
The stack installs the agent panel, console and wallboard itself. Nothing to upload by hand.
Alarms for ingest errors, the stream falling behind, API errors and failed usage reports, by email if you give an address.
Agent data deletion: remove everything Arena holds about one agent, from the console API or an admin script.
Quality streaks are assessed every night, with a bonus from the second clean day.
Wallboard TV links: a supervisor creates a sign-in-free link for a floor display, valid for 90 days and revocable.

title: First release
summary: The leaderboard, console and wallboard on live Amazon Connect data.
changes: Agent panel inside the Connect agent workspace: points, level, streak, badges and the team leaderboard.
Supervisor console: live leaderboard, flags for agents gone quiet, high volume with low quality, and evaluation auto-fails, plus a scoring mix you can tune.
Wallboard for a floor TV.
Scoring from the Connect agent event stream and Contact Lens evaluations. Quality outweighs speed, and an auto-fail removes points no setting can soften.
Challenges measured from Connect data, a reward catalog with supervisor approval, and kudos between teammates.
Sign-in through a user pool created in your account, or your own identity provider.
Everything deploys as one CloudFormation stack into your own AWS account.
